item.title: Chris Taylor says her time as an advocate prepared her for the Wisconsin Supreme Court
item.description: Wisconsin Supreme Court candidate Chris Taylor was a lobbyist for Planned Parenthood and a Democratic legislator before she became a judge. Her path reflects the changing nature of judicial races in Wisconsin.

item.title: Rising gas prices, delayed security lines may disrupt spring break travel
item.description: This year's spring break travel season comes amid rising gas prices and long security lines at major U.S. airports.

item.title: Wisconsin school board races get big boost in spending from national conservative group
item.description: Spending by the New York-based 1776 Project PAC is up 240 percent on Wisconsin races this year compared to 2025, according to records from the Wisconsin Ethics Commission.

item.title: Stewardship program likely to expire after Wisconsin Senate fails to take up bills
item.description: Conservation groups say Wisconsin will lose out on opportunities to set aside public lands and struggle to find funds to pursue that work as the state’s land purchase program is likely to expire in June.

item.title: Wisconsin Badgers win back-to-back national championships
item.description: On Sunday, the UW Badgers women's hockey team won 3-2 against number-one seeded Ohio State in the NCAA Frozen Four tournament.

item.title: 'Our attorneys are drowning': Public defender's office disappointed after court personnel bill dies
item.description: A Republican lawmaker and the state public defender's office are among those expressing dismay about the apparent death of a bill that would have added more court personnel.

item.title: Jason's classical picks: Trumpeters
item.description: "Drivetime Classics" host Jason Heilman writes about his favorite trumpeters, including classic and contemporary recordings.

item.title: State Democratic Party trounces GOP counterpart in February fundraising
item.description: New federal fundraising data shows Wisconsin's Democratic party brought in nine times as much as the state's Republican party last month.

item.title: AI is growing. Universities of Wisconsin wants to help you understand it.
item.description: AI technology is developing so fast, experts say advances are becoming hard to measure. Recognizing this, the Universities of Wisconsin has launched a free series of videos for people who need a starting point.

item.title: ‘Where the horror grows’: New anthology of scary story writers and places across Wisconsin
item.description: We learn about a new collection of 15 short horror stories by Wisconsin writers set across the state — from the Mississippi River to Door County and exurbs surrounding Milwaukee.
